review.headline: Busted cat in round two rides a 13-card nest to a first-place tie.
review.summary: Round 1 had no Meowfia. Under Banksia, players passed whispers from neighbour to neighbour, worked out that every egg was accounted for, and each threw one cheap card. In rounds 2 and 3 a lone House Cat (Casey, then Ellis) made up a Pigeon claim that the egg counts and an Owl report disproved within one or two beats, and the votes were nearly unanimous. Casey was caught in round 2, but she was Farm Vogelkop in round 3. She threw the big nest she had hoarded and banked 60, which tied her with Drew at 65.

rounds.recap: There were no Meowfia. Three Pigeon visits exactly explained Drew's +2 and Casey's +1, and Alex's Frog swap with Blair was confirmed by whisper. Everyone threw one card, nearly all Wilds. Alex went because his claim had only reached most players secondhand, and every thrown card was lost.

Casey, the House Cat, trusted Blair's wrong count that Drew was 'up 2' and claimed a Pigeon visit to Drew. Drew showed he was up 0, and his Owl report saw a House Cat and a Pelican visit Blair. Alex confirmed he was the real Pelican, so Casey was eggsecuted 4 to 0 by vote count.

Ellis, the House Cat, claimed he was a Pigeon whose visit to Drew the Pelican bounced back to his own nest. Casey pointed out that Blair's Owl, which was sent to Ellis, saw only a Pelican and a Vogelkop there, with no Pigeon. Every other claim was confirmed by someone else, so all four Farm players threw heavily at Ellis.

highlights.text: Drew's Owl report and Alex's real Pelican claim backed each other up. Together they left the House Cat as the only visitor to Blair nobody had claimed, and Casey's story fell apart in one speech.
Casey knew she was doomed and threw a single D7 at a Farm player, because the consolation rule would return it. It cost her nothing.
Casey caught Ellis with a sharp deduction: if Ellis really bounced home as a Pigeon, Blair's Owl would have seen a Pigeon at Ellis, and it did not.
Casey had been eggsecuted as the cat the round before. As Farm she threw 8 of her 13 cards, including two Wilds for extra votes, and banked 60 points.

confusions.what: Said Casey and Drew were both 'up 2' without allowing for the 2-card setup draw. Casey was really +1 and Drew +0.
Believed Blair's wrong count that Drew was up 2 and built a fake Pigeon visit to Drew on it, which Drew disproved at once.

Was unsure how the Pelican handles a visitor whose redirect would send them home. He guessed Ellis 'bounced back' and wasn't counted. In fact the engine never redirected Ellis at all, and his visit just stayed on Drew.
Built his cover story on the same unclear rule, a Pigeon redirected into its own nest. The Owl report could disprove that story.

design_notes: Round 1 was a dead round. With no Meowfia, the table proved it by beat 2, everyone threw a Wild, and Alex was eliminated at random. Rounds with zero cats need either rarer odds or some payoff for correctly calling 'no cat'. As it stands the only skill is throwing your cheapest card.

A lone House Cat had no believable claim. Nest counts are public, and Owl and Pelican reports cross-check visits, so a fake Pigeon claim leaves an egg that should exist but doesn't. Both cats were caught almost unanimously, and the highest Meowfia estimate any Farm player gave a Farm player in rounds 2 and 3 was 25%. Cats need a role that leaves no egg trace they can claim, or more noise in the information.

Pelican redirects are undefined when the visitor's target is the visitor themselves. Ellis went to Drew, who was visiting Ellis, and the engine quietly left the visit on Drew while Drew's egg bonus counted only Blair. Write a rule for this. Players spent a whole beat guessing at it.

A confused report has real effects: Casey drew 3 cards when her true gain was +1, and Ellis drew 1 when his was 0. Confusing someone can make their hand bigger, and Casey turned those extra cards into votes. On top of that, cards kept after a lost round become ammunition later, which is why the caught round-2 cat tied for first. That may be intended, but it means caught cats are barely punished.

Some cards did nothing. No second player was a Rabbit, so the Rabbit only showed up as a wrong name in a confused report. Banksia turned the 'public' speech into meaningless animal noises while neighbour-to-neighbour whispers carried all the real information. Poppy only made Blair keep his H9 by chance. Marigold's speeches worked well and caught the cat in a single pass.
